news.title: England name Women’s Under-20 World Cup squad despite boycott threat remaining
news.lede: England have named their squad for the Women’s Under-20 World Cup, despite the threat of a European boycott still hanging over the tournament. The event is due to kick off on September 5 with hosts Poland taking on Argentina but risks being the first FIFA tournament where European teams refuse to participate amid UEFA’s row with the global governing body over president Gianni Infantino’s plan to invite private investment in a company to run the World Cup. The Football Association is treating preparations for the tournament as ‘business as usual’, with coach Lydia Bedford’s under-20 squad due to convene at St George’s Park early next week. The Polish federation (PZPN) has also indicated to the Press Association that nothing has changed in its planning, but the threat of a boycott has not been lifted.

Manager Lydia Bedford has named her England squad for the upcoming Fifa U20s Women's World Cup amid ongoing threat of a boycott from European nations. There have been calls for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to resign following the controversy over the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal. It was aborted after widespread criticism from several confederations, led by Uefa, which has threatened a boycott of all Fifa competitions.

news.title: England to bid for World Cup 2038 or 2042 as Andy Burnham eyes huge tourism boost with Great Britain tournament
news.lede: GREAT BRITAIN is set to enter the race to host the World Cup in either 2038 or 2042. A bid backed by Prime Minister Andy Burnham is being considered as part of a plan to bring football‘s biggest tournament back to the UK for the first time since 1966. England hosted the World Cup 60 years ago, with Sir Alf Ramsey’s side famously lifting the trophy after beating West Germany in the final at Wembley. Now the tournament could return to these shores, with Burnham understood to view a World Cup as a major opportunity to drive investment, tourism and regeneration across the country.

news.title: Marko Stamenic: Swansea City midfielder gets love back after traumatic year
news.lede: Marko Stamenic has established himself as a key man in Swansea's midfield. Marko Stamenic says "the people around Swansea City" have helped him rediscover his love for football during his first year at the Championship club. Thursday marked 12 months since Stamenic said farewell to Nottingham Forest to take on the challenge of proving himself in the Championship at Swansea. The 24-year-old has achieved that feat despite the trauma brought by the sudden death of his father Nikola, who he calls the "main figure" in his development as a player, last October.
